claims.text: Preferential Cu segregation to FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle surfaces governs the onset and progression of premelting and melting.
Cu-rich surface regions have a lower effective melting point than the rest of the nanoparticle.
Cu-rich surface regions nucleate liquid domains.
Liquid domains originating in Cu-rich surface zones promote inward propagation of melting into the particle core.
As-synthesized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles contain minor intrinsic compositional heterogeneity, including subtle Cu enrichment at or near their surfaces.
Pre-annealing can homogenize the elemental distribution and minimize Cu segregation in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Thermal history can substantially affect HEA microstructure and phase evolution.
Cu has a lower elemental melting point than Fe, Ni, Cr, and Co.
Even modest surface segregation of Cu reduces the local melting temperature.
Cu-rich surface regions premelt while the remainder of the nanoparticle is still solid.
Liquid patches formed by surface premelting act as nucleation sites that facilitate surface-to-core melting.
As-synthesized nanoparticles will begin melting at a lower temperature than compositionally homogenized controls.
As-synthesized nanoparticles will exhibit spatially heterogeneous premelting localized at their surfaces.
As-synthesized nanoparticles will exhibit a two-step melting process.
Homogenized control nanoparticles will melt more uniformly and at a higher onset temperature.
The proposed behavior applies to approximately 10–50 nm particles, for which surface effects are significant.
Extreme heating rates or substantially different particle sizes may alter the melting response.
Synthesis conditions may affect the degree of segregation and the observed melting behavior.
Failure to observe earlier premelting at Cu-enriched regions, or observation of identical nonlocalized melting in both groups, would falsify the proposed Cu-segregation mechanism.
